newsitem.title: ITALY: ALPINE SKIING-COMPAGNONI SET FOR FIRST ITALIAN WIN.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-COMPAGNONI SET FOR FIRST ITALIAN WIN.

text.p: Olympic and world giant slalom champion Deborah Compagnoni, who in a decade on the women's World Cup Alpine skiing circuit has yet to win in her native Italy, was poised for victory on Sunday.

Compagnoni, winner of back-to-back giant slaloms in the German resort of Zwiesel at the end of last week, clocked one minute 21.45 seconds down a soft and fog-shrouded Olimpia delle Tofane piste in the first leg of a 60-gate giant.
Germany's Katja Seizinger, who won the first giant of the season in Soelden, Austria, was second fastest in 1:21.94 with Switzerland's Sonja Nef third quickest in 1:22.35.
Sweden's Pernilla Wiberg, the overall World Cup leader, was well-placed in fourth, 1.11 seconds behind Compagnoni.

Compagnoni, who decided not to race in Saturday's super-giant slalom to focus on trying to secure her third victory in a row, made two mistakes at the top of the piste but made up time on the lower part of the course.
"I got faster towards the end," she said. "I didn't feel too relaxed, I felt strangely pressured.
"The second leg will be better," she promised.
Victory in the second leg, starting at 1115 GMT, would be her fourth of the season. She won a slalom before Christmas.
Thicker fog settled over the middle of the course after Compagnoni and Seizinger had gone down and snow began to fall.
"The visibility wasn't the best," said Seizinger.
Italy's Isolde Kostner, who won Friday's downhill with Switzerland's Heidi Zurbriggen and then also took Saturday's super-G, missed a gate halfway down the leg.
"I lost the outside edge -- a technical error," she said.
Compatriot Sabina Panzanini, who won giants in Park City and Maribor, did not start due to a left Achilles problem.

Team officials said Panzanini had returned home to nearby Merano and had decided to rest. They said the injury, which Panzanini first noticed in Maribor and which flared up in Zwiesel, did not threaten her world championships.
The championships open in the Italian resort of Sestriere on February 2 and the host nation has high hopes for its women's team which has won seven World Cup races this season.
